answer: Several SOD1-ALS trials are relevant. The ATLAS study (NCT04856982) is enrolling presymptomatic SOD1 carriers with elevated neurofilament light and treats them with tofersen [s1]. Eligibility is open to adults aged 18-80 with a confirmed SOD1 mutation. The VALOR open-label extension (NCT03070119) continues to dose patients who completed VALOR; eligibility requires a baseline ALSFRS-R ≥ 30 [s2]. A separate program (NCT04768972) is evaluating ulefnersen, another SOD1-targeting ASO, in adults with confirmed SOD1 ALS aged 18-65 who can complete the swallowing test [s3]. Note that tofersen is investigational only and has not been FDA-approved [s1].

citations.title: ATLAS: A study of tofersen in presymptomatic adult carriers of SOD1 mutations
citations.snippet: This Phase 3 study is enrolling clinically presymptomatic adult carriers of a SOD1 mutation with biomarker evidence of disease activity (elevated CSF neurofilament light chain). Eligible participants are 18 years of age or older with a confirmed SOD1 mutation associated with high or complete penetrance.

citations.title: Open-label extension of VALOR (tofersen) for SOD1 ALS
citations.snippet: This open-label extension enrolls participants who completed the VALOR Phase 3 study. Eligibility includes prior completion of NCT02623699; there is no ALSFRS-R cutoff at entry to the extension.

citations.title: Study of ulefnersen (ION363/jacifusen) in fALS
citations.snippet: This Phase 3 study evaluates ulefnersen (ION363) in adults aged 18 years and older with FUS-mutation-associated ALS. SOD1 mutations are exclusion criteria.
